title: 9 Assassins

sources.label: HOW TO PLAY ★★★/9 Assassins Build In Auto Chess

body:
# 9 Assassins

Assassins leap over the enemy front line at the start of combat and land a
guaranteed critical strike on the backline; at nine Assassins that leap
*refreshes on every kill*, which effectively locks in a permanent maximum-crit
buff once the snowball starts. This guide follows the video's "high-roll"
approach rather than the classic hyper-roll: instead of forcing three-star
one-cost Assassins early, you build to nine Assassins with strong two-star
legendary carries (Magnus, Templar Assassin, Queen of Pain) and win the game on
itemization and timing. It's a safer route to a consistent top-four, at the cost
of a weaker mid game while you wait for your legendaries and items to come
online.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Magnus | 4 | Assassin, Centaur | Primary carry — his AoE stun sets up the whole team; the three-star target |
| Templar Assassin | 5 | Assassin, Elf | Highest-damage legendary carry; pierces multiple units and out-damages Queen of Pain |
| Queen of Pain | 5 | Assassin, Demon | Instant-cast nuke with pure damage from the Demon trait |
| Phantom Assassin | 4 | Assassin, Elf | Classic Battle Fury cleave carry |
| Pangolier | 4 | Assassin, Beast | Underrated burst — often out-damages a two-star Phantom Assassin with Battle Fury |
| Sand King | 3 | Aqir, Assassin | Frontline stun; sits forward to gain mana before leaping |
| Riki | 3 | Assassin, Satyr | Stealth smoke that silences and forces misses over the enemy backline |
| Slark | 2 | Assassin, Naga | Early two-star carry; excellent Mask of Madness holder |
| Spirit Breaker | 1 | Assassin, Tauren | Cheapest Assassin body; Mask of Madness gives it real attack speed |
| Leshrac | 5 | Centaur, Druid, God | Not an Assassin — added to pair with Magnus for the 2-Centaur Stampede |

Leshrac is the key off-synergy inclusion: he's a second Centaur, and 2-Centaur
Stampede makes Magnus charge to the most crowded enemy grid at the start of the
fight, so Magnus reliably lands his stun in the middle of the enemy team instead
of casting from the wrong position.

## Items

Offense first — the harder Assassins hit, the faster enemies die before they can
retaliate. Early, **Mask of Madness** on Slark or Spirit Breaker (attack speed +
lifesteal) carries the win streak. Mid game, **Bottle** and **Minotaur Horn**
give your stunners the mana to cast instantly on their leap. The carry items:
**Refresher Orb + Minotaur Horn** on Magnus so his stun casts twice back-to-back;
**Gleipnir** on Queen of Pain (it charges her to full mana at the fight's start
for an opening nuke); **Battle Fury** on Phantom Assassin or Pangolier for AoE
cleave; and **Havoc** on Templar Assassin for single-target pure damage. The
single biggest tier-five pickup is **Assault Cuirass** — its −armor aura
amplifies the whole team's physical damage by roughly a third and is the answer
to armored Warrior boards; put it on Magnus so it's always in the fight.

## Relics

**Forge** is the ideal second relic — it feeds the many purple items this build
depends on (Gleipnir, Refresher Orb, Battle Fury). **Leafy Essence** matters
after round 35 for higher levels and better odds at finding IO to three-star your
carries. **Mango Tree** is strong economy if you're comfortable with it, and the
**Greevil Egg** trick can bank a two-star legendary (e.g. Queen of Pain) early
by hatching it over several rounds while you stabilize.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Play a greedy win streak if you find an early two-star (Slark or Spirit Breaker),
banking gold and dismissing Humans (which removes three units from the tier-four
pool) to raise your Assassin odds. The target is level 9 before you commit to
rolling — that's your first real power spike into six then nine Assassins around
rounds 21–25. Keep carries at two-star through the mid game; only chase
three-stars after round 35, when IO makes them realistic. Magnus three-star is
the dream outcome (Refresher + Minotaur Horn + Assault Cuirass makes him a
game-ending permanent stun-lock), but a strong two-star Templar Assassin or Queen
of Pain wins plenty of games on its own.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Place the Assassins you *want* hit before they leap — Magnus and Sand King — on
the front line, so they take early damage, gain mana, and cast their stuns almost
immediately. Put Riki in the middle so its smoke covers where the rest of your
Assassins land, silencing and blinding that cluster. Keep the fragile nukers
(Queen of Pain, Templar Assassin) behind for safe mana gain. The build's hard
counter is nine Warriors: below 50% HP their armor doubles and they reflect pure
damage, so you physically cannot crit through them without armor reduction —
which is exactly why Assault Cuirass (and a pure-damage item like Havoc on
Templar Assassin) is mandatory. Gleipnir-style openings also lose value against
enemy Gleipnir/root that stops your leap, so lead with Queen of Pain's instant
cast to break those setups.
